items.criterion: A forecast array is written to the declared submission path.
items.judgment: EFFECT: /submission/forecast.npy exists and loads as a real-valued numpy array; an object dtype, a missing file or an unreadable one scores zero with reason submission_malformed.

items.criterion: No forecast consumed an observation at or after its own origin.
items.judgment: EFFECT: The run record's declared maximum consumed index for each forecast origin is strictly below that origin. This is red line 1 and it is checked against the record the run produced, never against a post-hoc scan.

items.criterion: Forecast values sit inside the envelope the shipped history makes plausible.
items.judgment: EFFECT: Every forecast value is finite and lies within the min/max of the agent-visible training channel widened by its own standard deviation; a forecast outside that envelope is a degenerate or mis-scaled submission rather than a weak one.

items.criterion: The forecast covers exactly the graded forecast origins at the bound horizon.
items.judgment: EFFECT: The flattened forecast length equals the number of graded targets the verifier holds; a short array cannot be padded and a long one cannot be truncated to fit.

items.criterion: The agent declares its own lookback and split budget for the graded run.
items.judgment: EFFECT: The run record carries an agent-authored declaration naming the lookback window and the total leaf-split budget used. The declaration is graded, not the harness's own measurement, so the check cannot be satisfied by a field the harness writes.

items.criterion: The skill score against persistence clears the published bar through the ramp.
items.judgment: EFFECT: 1 - MAE(model)/MAE(persistence) over the private future window, mapped through the floor-to-knee ramp. UNMEASURED AT PHASE 0: the ramp constants are null, so this check raises ConstantUnmeasured rather than returning a score.

items.criterion: The validation policy the agent declares respects time order.
items.judgment: EFFECT: The declared split policy names an ordered holdout and no shuffled or randomly permuted fold. CTL-LEAK targets exactly this and must be rejected: a shuffled split is a red line scoring zero, not a lever with a bounded worth.
